key_insight: SequenTx uses a virtual-cell-inspired simulation of tumour cellular states plus reinforcement learning to design adaptive sequences of drug treatments that steer tumour evolution rather than react to it.
problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of selecting time-varying, multi-step therapies that anticipate and counteract therapy-induced tumour evolution and state transitions.
method: Construct a dynamic tumour model that represents cellular states and therapy-induced state transitions (virtual-cell-inspired simulator).
Train a reinforcement learning agent to optimize sequential treatment policies within the simulated evolving tumour landscape.
Evaluate policies by simulating long-term tumour composition and therapeutic outcomes to identify robust, evolution-aware treatment schedules.
impact: Demonstrates how RL can be combined with mechanistic simulators to solve complex, sequential decision problems in biomedical domains; useful for ML practitioners building policy-learning systems for evolving environments and model-based policy evaluation.
visual_elements: Schematic of the virtual-cell state graph showing cellular phenotypes and therapy-induced transitions.
Diagram of the RL loop: simulator (tumour) → agent (policy) → treatment actions → updated tumour states.
Timeline plot comparing sequential treatment schedules with changes in tumour composition over time.
Heatmap or bar chart of policy outcomes (e.g., tumour burden or resistant fraction) across different strategies.
paper_title: Reinforcement learning-based design of sequential drug treatment targeting the evolving tumour landscape with SequenTx
paper_authors: Xiaohan Chen, Yue Deng, Xingbo Yang, Ying Zhang, Yuting Huang
